findings.reasoning: Coordinate validation and URL encoding are thoroughly implemented. `isValidCoordinate` validates against null/undefined, checks `Number.isFinite` (blocking NaN and Infinity), enforces valid geographic bounds (lat: -90..90, lng: -180..180), and filters null-island coordinates. Both `calculateHaversineDistance` and `generateGoogleMapsDirUrl` defensively check coordinates before proceeding. Furthermore, `generateGoogleMapsDirUrl` formats coordinates with `.toFixed(6)` and constructs queries using standard WHATWG `URL` and `URLSearchParams.set`, which automatically percent-encodes values and eliminates the possibility of query parameter or protocol injection.

Static analysis of the provided snippet reveals no pending delete queue, debounce mechanisms, or scheduled deletion timers (such as setTimeout/setInterval). Deletion state is tracked via standard boolean/ID flags (deletingTripId, isDeleting) for dialog visibility. Furthermore, all registered lifecycle effects properly register and unregister window event listeners during cleanup, leaving no unhandled timers or unmount desynchronization vulnerabilities.

In React/JSX, string variables rendered in the DOM are automatically HTML-escaped by default, preventing stored XSS. Within TransitSegmentConnector.tsx, 'custom_note' is never rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML, nor is it interpolated into any href attribute or unescaped HTML context (it is only evaluated truthy/falsy to display a small status dot indicator and bound to standard form state). Therefore, no XSS vulnerability or unsanitized link trigger exists.

The component uses standard Radix UI Dialog primitives (@/components/ui/dialog) rather than a custom BottomSheet. Radix UI Dialog natively encapsulates focus trapping, portal rendering, and outside click/escape dismiss logic. The proposed issue describes a speculative or non-existent BottomSheet upgrade, and static inspection reveals no unhandled event bubbling or portal escape defect in the provided snippet.
